title: Entropy inequalities, recovery boundaries and thermal entanglement

items.title: Dimensionless entropy, mutual and conditional information
items.statement:
All Hilbert spaces in this item are nonzero and finite-dimensional over $\mathbb C$. A density operator $\rho$ on $H$ is a Hermitian positive semidefinite endomorphism with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Its dimensionless von Neumann entropy, in nats, is

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\log\lambda_j,$$

where $\lambda_j$ are the eigenvalues of $\rho$, the logarithm is natural, and $0\log0:=0$. For any positive semidefinite endomorphisms $X,Y$ on one finite-dimensional $H$, let $\operatorname{supp}X:=(\ker X)^\perp$. Define

$$D(X\|Y):=\operatorname{Tr}(X\log X)-\operatorname{Tr}(X\log Y)$$

when $\operatorname{supp}X\subseteq\operatorname{supp}Y$, taking each logarithm spectrally on its positive support and setting zero-eigenvalue contributions to zero; set $D(X\|Y):=+\infty$ otherwise. For density operators this is the finite-dimensional quantum relative entropy in nats.

For a density operator $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, define $\rho_A:=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B:=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, where in orthonormal product bases $\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_B R\bigr)_{ii'}=\sum_jR_{(i,j),(i',j)}$ and the first factor is retained. Define

$$I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a density operator $\rho_{ABC}$ on $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, define

$$\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_C\rho_{ABC},\qquad \rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{ABC},\qquad \rho_B:=\operatorname{Tr}_A(\operatorname{Tr}_C\rho_{ABC}),$$

where each partial trace contracts the indicated tensor factor and retains the other factors in their displayed order.

$$I(A:C\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{ABC}),$$

using the partial traces in the displayed factor order. For any fixed positive conversion factor $k_B$ with units J/K, the corresponding physical entropy is $S_{\mathrm{phys}}(\rho):=k_BS(\rho)$; no numerical value of $k_B$ is specified here.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, §5.2.1, author-hosted manuscript
Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, Chapter 11, §§11.1 and 11.6, second-edition prepublication full text

items.title: Conditional mutual information and finite channel monotonicity
items.statement:
Let $H_A,H_B,H_C$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a density operator on $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$. With $S$ and $I(A:C\mid B)$ as defined in [[def-qsmx-information-conventions]],

$$I(A:C\mid B)_\rho=S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{ABC})\ge0.$$

Also let $d,e\ge1$ and let $\Phi:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_e(\mathbb C)$ be a finite completely positive trace-preserving map. For all positive semidefinite $X,Y\in M_d(\mathbb C)$,

$$D(\Phi(X)\|\Phi(Y))\le D(X\|Y),$$

where $D$ is the support-sensitive finite-dimensional quantum relative entropy: it equals $\operatorname{Tr}(X\log X)-\operatorname{Tr}(X\log Y)$ when $\operatorname{supp}X\subseteq\operatorname{supp}Y$, and $+\infty$ otherwise. These are finite-dimensional mathematical statements. The channel inequality is one-sided and asserts no equality condition, recovery map, or infinite-dimensional extension.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, Theorem 5.35 and proof; Theorem 5.36 and proof, author-hosted manuscript
Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, Chapter 11, Theorems 11.7.1 and 11.8.1; Corollary 11.9.1, second-edition prepublication full text

items.title: Boundary energy bounds thermal mutual information
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H_A,\mathcal H_B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces. Let $H_A=H_A^*$ act on $\mathcal H_A$, let $H_B=H_B^*$ act on $\mathcal H_B$, and let $H_{\partial}=H_{\partial}^*$ act on $\mathcal H_A\otimes\mathcal H_B$. Set

$$H:=H_A\otimes I_B+I_A\otimes H_B+H_{\partial}.$$

For $\beta>0$, define $Z_\beta:=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})$ and the finite Gibbs density $\rho_\beta:=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$. Then

$$I(A:B)_{\rho_\beta}\le 2\beta\|H_{\partial}\|_{\mathrm{op}},$$

where $I(A:B)$ uses dimensionless entropy in nats and $\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=\sup_{\|v\|=1}\|Kv\|$ is the operator norm. If a specified family of lattice partitions additionally has a declared boundary-size count $|\partial A|$ (the number of crossing interaction terms) and satisfies $\|H_{\partial}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C|\partial A|$ for a specified $C\ge0$, then $I(A:B)_{\rho_\beta}\le 2\beta C|\partial A|$ for that family; no lattice geometry or boundary-scaling hypothesis is otherwise assumed. When $H$ is measured in joules, $\beta$ has units J$^{-1}$ and $C$ has units J, so the bound is dimensionless.

references.title: Michael M. Wolf, Frank Verstraete, Matthew B. Hastings, and J. Ignacio Cirac, Area laws in quantum systems: mutual information and correlations, arXiv:0704.3906v2, §Mutual information and correlations
Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.4, finite-dimensional entropy and Gibbs free-energy identity
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, §§5.2.1–5.2.3, author-hosted manuscript

items.title: Identical marginals and unequal quantum information
items.statement:
Let $H_A=H_B=\mathbb C^2$ with the fixed orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ on each factor. Define the Bell density

$$\rho_\Phi=|\Phi\rangle\langle\Phi|,\qquad |\Phi\rangle=(|00\rangle+|11\rangle)/\sqrt2,$$

and the computational-basis-dephased density

$$\rho_{\mathrm{diag}}=\tfrac12|00\rangle\langle00|+\tfrac12|11\rangle\langle11|.$$

Both have marginals $I_2/2$, but their dimensionless mutual informations differ: $I(A:B)_{\rho_\Phi}=2\log2$ and $I(A:B)_{\rho_{\mathrm{diag}}}=\log2$. The displayed formula defines the dephased state; no measurement or experimental outcome is asserted.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, §5.2, author-hosted manuscript
Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, Chapter 11, §11.6, second-edition prepublication full text
